display_name: Attorney General Law (Opinions, Representation and Supervision), 5786-2026: every section, every cross-reference as a typed value, the indirect amendment as before-and-after text

run.method: one agent working alone from the lead's brief (the Israeli defect hunt); tests written by hand from the text before the modules were run; three mutations of rule modules were each caught by the tests

seat: the individual to whom the Law is applied: a party to, or facing, a court proceeding in which the State takes a side, or a person whose matter an official decides (il41-seat.l4). A second layer, the recipient of an opinion (il41-seat-recipient.l4), follows the lead's brief and is not a commons seat.

language.note: Identifiers and comments are English. Hebrew from the sources appears only in `-- tag:N |` comments generated by tools/srcquote.py from line N of a deposited source, and in four string literals that tools/hebcheck.py checked occur verbatim in a deposited source.

source.authority: aid: the Knesset's unofficial text (docx converted with textutil); its words compared with the official pages as multisets and the pages read by eye (NOTES.md section 3)

official_source.authority: official publication (the Knesset's PDF of Sefer HaChukim 3550), read from the page images; page 3's text layer carries every word twice

other_sources.authority: aid; CONSOLIDATION-ONLY except ss 1 and 2(a), read from the official page image (tag com-sh)
aid (a Wikisource page of the new Law itself)
aid (the bill as put to the second and third readings; pages 2 to 6, the text of the Law as submitted)

scope: Every section of the Law (1 to 20): ss 1, 4, 5 (opinions), 6 to 12 (representation), 13 to 15, 17 to 20 as rules or typed values; s 2 and s 3(a) as quoted text only; s 16 as the typed before-and-after text of the amendment; every cross-reference (24 inside the Law, 6 outside it) as a typed value a test checks. Not encoded: the text of the cited laws beyond what is cited (the Ordinance, the State as Litigant Law, the Appointments Law, the Complaints Commissioner Law are typed at the point of citation only), the reservations offered at the second reading, and the Knesset's Rules.

forks.F1: Seat: the individual first (commons rulings of 2026-10-18 and 2026-10-21); a second layer for the recipient of an opinion because the lead's brief suggested it, labelled as the brief's choice, not a commons seat.
forks.F2: The words quoted in comments come from the Knesset's unofficial text, a logical-order file; the official PDF cannot be quoted mechanically (visual order; page 3 doubled). The pages were read by eye and the words compared as multisets.
forks.F3: s 20: 'within 30 days from the day of its commencement': whether the commencement day is day one. Declined by default; two readings kept by name.
forks.F4: s 5(b): the Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee is read as the committee for an opinion on State security or foreign relations, instead of the Constitution, Law and Justice Committee. Rejected: either at the Government's choice.
forks.F5: The subjects of the citing sides of the references in ss 16 and 20 are inferred (those sections describe their targets in no words).
forks.F6: s 12(a): the three exclusions are alternatives (any one takes the matter out of Chapter B). Rejected: all three together.
forks.F7: s 9: the Government's power to choose another lawyer is read as given where the Attorney General has given notice under s 8 or the minister concerned considers that the position is not or will not be properly presented through him; a decision without either is not within it, so the Attorney General presents. Rejected: a power with no such condition.
forks.F8: s 15(c)(3): where the Attorney General considers that the step might harm an important public interest, the account the Minister asked for under (2) goes to the Commissioner and not to the Minister. Rejected: to both.

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this encoding against the source, and no independent tester has run yet. Every expected value was worked by hand from the text before it was asserted. A mutation check was run on three rules (s 4 default, s 10(a) bar, s 20 count) and each mutation was caught; no wider mutation check was run.

check.note: every module has the same four counts on the main build; no module declares a failed assertion.
